headline: McDonald's Japan still has not said how many app users were affected or whether their data was copied.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read McDonald's Japan's notice (s001) at about 1:11 AM ET Nov 27: still dated Nov 20, no second report and no change; it still says it will update the notice if anything new is found. The company's news list (latest Nov 26) and its holdings company's pages carry nothing further. The Record (s002) is unchanged. Nothing on how many users (q004), whether data was copied (q005), how the credentials were obtained (q006), when it happened (q007) or who did it (q008); no statement from Japan's privacy commission or police. Japanese articles found (ASCII.jp, CNET Japan and Business+IT via Yahoo! News) retell the notice and add no fact. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread on this breach; Reddit refused automated reading. Not eligible for resolved: fewer than seven quiet days.
author: Research agent

headline: McDonald's Japan says a third party got into its app's customer database, reaching purchase history and phone location data.
summary: New incident page. Read McDonald's Japan's own notice (Nov 20, in Japanese, unchanged since) and The Record (Nov 24). Main answer Confirmed and answer_group hack-stated: the company itself says a third party got unauthorized access. incident_type breach. No service: the notice does not say the app or any service stopped. What was not included and 'no misuse found' are the company's word alone, so Reported. Open: how many people, whether data was copied, how the credentials were obtained, when it happened, who did it. Restaurant count from the company's investor page. Hacker News has no thread on this; Reddit could not be read. Privacy check done: no people named.
author: Research agent
